messages.author: 8cb6dd30cf9761ae
messages.subject: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
Hi all,

 I'm having a problem with SVGs exported with ggsave, and wonder whether anyone might have a suggestion. The SVGs use the <def> element, to define common elements, and these common elements are assigned IDs to refer to them. The problem is that while these IDs are unique within each plot, they are not consistent between plots. The result is that if more than one ggsave generated SVG is included in a web-page, then the IDs collide, messing up the plots.

Does anyone know of a way to control the generation of these IDs, say to given them a unique prefix per plot? (Maybe this is not a ggplot2 specific question after all ...)

Thanks in advance for any suggestions,


Jony

messages.author: 8cb6dd30cf9761ae
messages.subject: Re: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
Hi Ista,

 almost any SVG generated by ggplot will do. For example running:

qplot(mpg, hp, color = factor(cyl), data = mtcars)

when exported to SVG will have a <def> section with troublesome IDs (#glyph0-0 etc).

Embedding the images in an iframe could be a workaround, but I don't think it's really the right solution.

Speaking of workarounds, for my application I took to replacing the IDs with GUIDs. The code for this is here: 

https://github.com/JonyEpsilon/gg4clj/blob/acc06766073491b42fea006ff5beb249b9e06afa/src/gg4clj/core.clj#L97

It's in Clojure, but should be easy to translate if anyone has the need.

Overall, though, I think the best solution would be to generate SVGs with unique IDs. I'm pretty inexperienced in R, so I'm not sure I have anything useful to offer on that front I'm afraid.

Yours,


Jony

messages.author: 8cb6dd30cf9761ae
messages.subject: Re: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
No problem. To reproduce run:

library(ggplot2)
qplot(mpg, hp, color = factor(cyl), data = mtcars)

ggsave("test1.svg")
qplot(mpg, hp, color = factor(gear), data = mtcars)
ggsave("test2.svg")

And then put both of the SVG files in the same HTML page. I've attached a zipped HTML file where I've done that. You'll note that the legend on the second plot is broken, as the glyph*-* IDs are colliding with those in the first plot.


Jony

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
Thanks Jony,

If I were doing this I would include these images in the html in a way
that does not require unique IDs.

<html>
<head></head>
<body>
<object id="testPlot1" type="image/svg+xml" data="test1.svg"
width="600" height="600">
<param name="src" value="ovals.svg">
</object>
<object id="testPlot2" type="image/svg+xml" data="test2.svg"
width="600" height="600">
<param name="src" value="ovals.svg">
</object>
</body>
</html>

Seems to work pretty well.

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 8cb6dd30cf9761ae
messages.subject: Re: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
Hi Ista,

 yes, I think that is another fine workaround, although I'd note that it's not always possible to rely on external resources (and in my case isn't). Data URIs can sometimes provide a way out of that, but my experience is that they can be _very_ slow for any non-trivial amount of data.

For context, I'm embedding the generated SVGs in Gorilla REPL documents (http://gorilla-repl.org). This is a HTML-based application, rather than a document, which is what leads to the rather specific requirements.

I think the ideal solution, which could adapt to all use cases would be the ability to specify a unique prefix for the generated IDs, or something similar.


Jony

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
I'm not entirely sure what you mean by relying on external resources.
Hopefully someone will prove me wrong, but I don't think there are any
facilities for specifying id prefixes when writing to the svg device
in R, so your options as I see them are 1) include the svg files in
such a way as to not require unique IDs, 2) post-process the svg
files, or 3) hack R's svg device to write unique IDs.

Option 1 is by far the easiest. Option 2 can be as simple as

sed -i 's/glyph/f1glyph/' test1.svg
sed -i 's/glyph/f2glyph/' test2.svg

depending on your platform, or perhaps

system.time({write(gsub("glyph", "f1glyph", x1),
file = "test1_fixed.svg")})

if you need to do it within R. Option 3 is beyond my capabilities.

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 8cb6dd30cf9761ae
messages.subject: Re: Colliding SVG ids
parts:
Thanks Ista.

By "relying on external resources" I mean that in your example, the SVG data is accessed through separate resources than the HTML code i.e. they have their own URL (and are probably in their own files). That isn't always possible, or at least efficient, especially when the data is created dynamically in an HTML app.

The code I posted earlier is my take on option 2. Not all IDs start with "glyph" ("path" and "pattern" are ones I've also seen), so I replace all IDs, but it's essentially the same approach. It works well enough.


Jony
